newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Cerro Vanguardia gold mine cost $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Cerro Vanguardia gold mine cost $200 mln.

text.p: The Cerro Vanguardia gold mine being developed in southern Argentina will cost $200 million to build, the site's owners said Friday.

Cerro Vanguardia is being developed by Minera Mincorp SA, owned 50 percent each by Luxembourg-based Minorco and local conglomerate Perez Companc. It is widely touted by other foreign miners as a star project and has triggered a modest gold rush in the Patagonian province of Santa Cruz.

"The total spending in exploration and studies will come to $41 million and the construction will cost about $200 million," said Roberto Traba, president of Santa Cruz province mining company Fomecruz.

Traba told Reuters that Fomecruz and the national government had been given copies of the final feasibility study and that construction of the open-pit mine could start in the second half of October. He said the mine would produce around 220,000 ounces a year of gold and 50 tonnes of silver.
Under a joint-venture deal, Fomecruz will receive 6.6 percent of Cerro Vanguardia's eventual mine output and 7.5 percent of net profits.

Minera Mincorp general manager Roger Davey said that he could not yet comment on the cost of the project or how much the mine would produce. But he said that Mincorp's partners had approved the feasibility study.

Mincorp is now adjudicating the contract for construction of the mine, Davey said. When asked when building would begin, he replied "I would not like to speak for the contractors as to when they would begin construction." He declined to say which companies were competing in the construction tender.

Sources close to the project forecast in March that the mine would be in operation by 1999 if construction began this August. They said production would most likely be in the form of a dore bullion mix of gold and silver, with 2,000 tonnes of ore being processed a day.
The sources said that reserves at the site totalled nine million tonnes of ore, with 10 grams of gold and 110 grams of silver a tonne.

Cerro Vanguardia is one of the biggest mining projects to be set up in Argentina since the free-market government of President Carlos Menem swept away regulations and restrictions that kept foreign miners away for decades. Word of the project's success has helped attract more than 20 international prospectors to Santa Cruz.
